articles.title: Reset a locked-out account password
steps: Confirm the user's identity (employee ID + manager name) before touching the account.
Check if the account is locked due to repeated failed attempts (Admin Console > Users > Security).
If locked, clear the lockout and send a password-reset link to the user's on-file email.
Ask the user to sign in with the new password within 15 minutes, before the reset link expires.
If the lockout recurs immediately after reset, escalate — it may indicate a compromised credential, not a forgotten password.

articles.title: User cannot complete multi-factor authentication
steps: Ask which MFA method the user is using (authenticator app, SMS, hardware key).
Check the MFA provider's status page for an active outage before assuming a user-side issue.
If the user's device/app is out of sync, guide them to re-sync time in the authenticator app settings.
If the user lost their MFA device, do not disable MFA yourself — this requires the access-review process (see KB-003).

articles.title: User needs access or permission to a resource
steps: Identify the exact resource (report, folder, database, tool) and the permission level requested.
Check whether the user's role already includes this entitlement (Admin Console > Roles).
If it does not, this requires a permission change — the assistant may only recommend it; a human must approve and apply it.
Document the business justification given by the user for the access-review audit trail.

articles.title: Power BI report is blank or fails to refresh
steps: Confirm whether the issue is the whole report (blank/won't load) or a single visual.
Check the dataset's last successful refresh time in the Power BI service (Settings > Refresh history).
If the refresh failed, open the refresh history error detail — most failures are a source-credential expiry.
If credentials expired, the data-source connection needs re-authentication — flag for the report owner, do not modify shared credentials directly.
If the report loads but a visual is blank, check for an active filter/slicer excluding all data.

articles.title: Database query is slow, timing out, or failing
steps: Get the exact query or stored procedure name and the error message/timeout duration reported.
Check current database load and any active blocking sessions or deadlocks (DBA dashboard).
If a deadlock is present, note the two contending transactions — this is a candidate for the DBA team, not a self-serve fix.
If it's a timeout on a specific report/query, check whether an index or query-plan change is needed before recommending a code fix.

articles.title: Data appears missing, duplicated, or incorrect
steps: Get a specific example: which record, which field, and what value was expected vs. shown.
Check the source system directly to see if the discrepancy originates upstream or in this report/view.
If duplicates are present, identify the shared key causing the duplication before recommending any deletion.
Never modify or delete data directly — document findings and recommend the correction for a human to apply.

articles.title: General how-to / technical question
steps: Identify the specific tool or workflow the question is about.
Check internal documentation and prior tickets for an existing answer before drafting a new one.
If no documented answer exists, note this as a documentation gap rather than guessing.
